d: Delicious gardens, on one side shady avenues, statues, and fountains, and more shops of various drinks. Gentiluomini, who go around, Madama la Rose, and Traversen, then Alberto, who come over.
Don Pomponio in rich dress, and loaded, two Lackhe, who follow him, said (as above).
Elegant room in the inn of Filippo, corresponding to various apartments. Filippo, then Doralice, and Anselmo.
Lisetta dressed in all elegance.
Alberto, and sayings.
Doralice, then Alberto.
Alberto, then Don Pomponio.
Lisetta, then Filippo, and Doralice listening, then Alberto from the room and said.
Madame la Rose, then Doralice, then Pomponio, and one of his Lacche.
Filippo from the inside, and sayings.
Lisetta, that's it.
Madame, Traversen, Doralice, Anselmo, and Alberto.
Lisetta, and Pomponio, Filippo da quakero, ascended under thick wig that descends on the shoulders and eyes, followed by other Quakeri.
Room in the same inn. Madame La Rose, Traversen, Anselmo, Doralice.
Alberto, who saw Traversen in arms with Doralice, then Monsieur Traversen returning.
Filippo, then Lisetta.
Alberto alone.
Filippo, then Alberto.
Garden with rustic cottage with door, workable. Pomponio with a Lacche that brings him a measuring sword.
Alberto, and sayings.
Room. Lisetta and Doralice, then Madame la Rose.
Pomponius, and sayings.
Filippo, then Pomponio.

Room vaguely illuminated for dance party. Maschere's Choir, Lisetta masked as Turkish, then Alberto masked of the same way, then Doralice with dress similar to that of Lisetta; later Filippo dressed as Alberto, and finally Pomponio ridiculedly even him.
Anselmo, Traversen, then Pomponio from opposite scenes, then Madame la Rose, and finally Filippo with Lisetta, and Alberto with Doralice.
